what_happened: The job to track verification cost, catches, false positives and escapes in status was rejected at the final verdict. One of 8 acceptance criteria was unmet: the unit test in crates/athena-core that builds Records with rejected and passed verifications, job totals, an overruled rejection and a landed job later reverted, and asserts the counts. It must fail when the computation is stubbed out and pass with it. The verifier gave one blocker: the false-positive count is always 0 on real records. Both conditions it tests are impossible, and the existing overrule detection is not reused (status/verification.rs:51-53). No checks are listed as failed.
cause: A new status measure was built and tested on hand-built Records fixtures and never replayed on the real records or compared with an independent source. The fixture's overruled rejection could satisfy conditions that real records never produce, so the test passed while the real false-positive count stayed 0. Nothing required the measure to reuse the existing overrule detection or to show a non-zero value on real history before the final verdict. The same status-measure job family keeps failing this way.
other_causes: The test fixture's overruled-rejection shape does not match what the real writers produce, so the fixture and the real records disagree.
The producer was not told about this recurring status-measure gap, which earlier cases had already recorded.
open_hypotheses: Whether the producer looked at how overrules are recorded in real history, or wrote the conditions from the request's wording alone.
Whether the stub-out test would have caught the always-zero count if the fixture had used real record shapes.
contradictions: The unmet criterion asks for a unit test on built Records, not a real-records run. The earlier cases in this class failed on real-records criteria, so this case differs in what the criterion required.
prevention: Add a check that runs every new status measure over the real records (history.json, recorded invocations) before the job counts as done. It would fail a measure that is zero where an independent count is not zero. It would also require measures built on a recorded event, such as an overrule, to reuse the existing detection for it. Show the producer this check for any job that adds a status measure.
proposed_request: Fix the verification false-positive count in `athena status`, in crates/athena-core/src/status/verification.rs. The count is always 0 on real records because the conditions it tests cannot occur. Make it reuse the existing overrule detection so a rejection later overruled counts as a false positive. Acceptance: (1) Running `athena status --snapshot` on the real records shows a verification line with total verifier cost, rejections caught, false positives and escapes. The false-positive count equals the number of rejections the existing overrule detection finds in history.json, and that number is non-zero if history.json holds any overruled rejection. (2) A unit test in crates/athena-core builds Records from the shapes the real writers produce, with rejected and passed verifications, job totals, an overruled rejection and a landed job later reverted. It asserts the four counts and fails when the computation is stubbed out. (3) Evidence for each behavior criterion cites commands that ran (D43). (4) cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test pass. (5) Add the CHANGELOG.md entry.
